elements.element: Customer has no minimum purchase or volume commitment.
elements.evidence: The rendered Section 4.2.3(ii) now reads "which shall be no more than $120 million, with no minimum amount," deleting the prior "no less than $110 million and" floor. PB's election of the Elected Total Amount is therefore uncapped on the downside, and no other retained language in the cited text imposes a floor on what PB must elect or fund.

elements.element: Customer pays only for usage or ordered Services.
elements.evidence: Retained Section 6.2 scales PB's Approval Payments by "a fraction, the numerator of which is such actual amount of Development Costs paid or incurred by SFJ hereunder ... and the denominator of which is One Hundred Twenty Million U.S. Dollars ($120,000,000.00)," so PB's payment obligation tracks the funding actually drawn rather than a notional committed amount. With the floor removed, the elected/actual amount is entirely PB's ordered quantum.

elements.element: The commitment is limited to the current 12-month term.
elements.evidence: Nothing in the rendered language ties any commitment to a 12-month period; the Elected Total Amount is a one-time election made after the Successful Phase 3 Interim Analysis and runs through the Development Term (Effective Date to the later of Clinical Trial Completion Dates / conclusion of Regulatory Approval efforts). Not required, since the preferred level is complete.

elements.element: Customer may reduce the commitment on 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: No reduction-on-notice mechanic was added or exists; once PB "shall notify SFJ in writing" of the Elected Total Amount, the clause provides no right to revise it downward on 30 days' notice. Not required, since the preferred level is complete.

elements.element: Any shortfall is handled through a true-up rather than a penalty.
elements.evidence: The only true-up in the cited text is the Section 6.2 recalculation of Approval Payments where Regulatory Approval is obtained in one jurisdiction while other Development Costs are still being incurred; it is not a shortfall true-up, and the at-will exit (300% of Development Costs incurred) remains a penalty-style payment. Not required, since the preferred level is complete.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: the deletion of the $110 million floor plus the express "with no minimum amount" removes any minimum election obligation, and retained Section 6.2 already ensures PB's Approval Payments are proportionate to the Development Costs actually paid or incurred by SFJ.

Minimality holds: the edit strikes only the words "no less than $110 million and" within the target sentence, retains the $120 million ceiling, the election mechanic, the PB Costs formula, the quarterly payment schedule and the overrun/use-of-funds allocation, and the added five-word clarifier is the operative implementation of the no-minimum element rather than a model-language extra.

Intent is preserved: the $120,000,000.00 denominator in Section 6.2 is untouched, no cross-reference is left dangling, and no defined term (Elected Total Amount, PB Costs, Development Costs) becomes undefined.

Drafting watch-item (not a defect requiring repair): because the Elected Total Amount is stated to be "inclusive of all Development Costs paid or incurred since the Effective Date," an election below the sum of items (a)-(e) simply yields no PB Costs payment under the retained formula; if SFJ raises this, consider a short clarifier that the PB Costs payment is zero (not negative) where the Elected Total Amount does not exceed that sum, rather than reinstating any floor.

Fallback is deliberately not reached (no 12-month limit, no 30-day reduction right, no shortfall true-up), which is acceptable here because the preferred checklist is fully met; the margin comment correctly reserves the fallback for negotiation without promising it in operative text.
